junk_imagery.evidence: All imagery appears to be custom animation.

decorative_mascot.evidence: The mascot actively changes numbers on a billboard (hook@0.3), adds crosses to a memorial (seg2:start), and paints a crosswalk (seg3:start).

bare_number_card.evidence: Numbers are presented on a billboard that the mascot interacts with (hook@0.3), or as percentages next to visual elements like crosses (seg2:end), or as a painted stripe on a crosswalk (seg3:end).

dead_air.evidence: The longest static stretch is 0.0s, and the maximum frozen run is 0.7s, well below the 4s threshold.

empty_void.evidence: The frames are well-composed with backgrounds and foreground elements, no large dead black spaces.

unreadable.evidence: All text is clear, high contrast, and not cut off or obscured.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: The data demonstration for traffic deaths uses a billboard mechanic, which is clear but a somewhat generic way to show changing numbers.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The visual metaphor for showing year-over-year totals is functional but not highly unique.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Develop a more bespoke and surprising visual metaphor for demonstrating changing traffic death totals over time.

depictions.note: Mascot updates numbers on a billboard, a clear but somewhat generic mechanic for showing changing totals.
Continues the billboard mechanic from seg0, emphasizing the pedestrian outlier.
Mascot adds crosses to a memorial, directly representing pedestrian deaths and visually conveying the rise before numbers appear.
Mascot paints a red stripe on a crosswalk, using the crosswalk itself as a direct visual metaphor for the percentage of pedestrian deaths.

grades.one_line: The video effectively demonstrates the disproportionate rise in pedestrian deaths with engaging visual metaphors and mascot interaction.
problems: The billboard mechanic used in the first two segments, while effective, is a relatively common visual for displaying changing numbers and could be more innovative.
fixes: Explore more unique and bespoke visual metaphors for showing year-over-year data changes, especially for the initial presentation of overall traffic deaths.
